name: distance-immigration
title: Isolation reduces colonization; migration conserves individuals
question:
Does the distance-decaying migration kernel (migration_rate = 1/(1+distance))
reproduce the immigration side of MacArthur-Wilson theory — more isolated
islands receive fewer colonists — and does inter-island migration conserve
individuals exactly?
hypothesis:
Because the per-pair migration probability falls as 1/(1+distance), an island
that is on average farther from the others should receive fewer immigrants per
generation, so immigration received should correlate negatively with mean
distance. Separately, every emigration moves exactly one individual to exactly
one other island, so the archipelago-wide net migration flux must be exactly
zero (individuals are conserved by the coupler).
objective:
Over a seed ensemble, measure (a) the across-island correlation of immigration
received with mean distance to the other islands, and (b) the total net
migration flux summed over all islands and generations.
description:
Faithful port of IslandManager.simulate's migration loop: for each ordered
island pair (i, j), with probability migration_rate(d_ij) a random present
species moves one individual i -> j. This study isolates the MigrationProcess
coupler: it validates the distance kernel (the colonization/immigration side of
island biogeography) and the conservation law that makes migration a genuine
exchange rather than a source/sink. Islands are held at full occupancy so the
measured immigration reflects the geometry, not transient population collapse.

expected_behavior.name: isolation-reduces-immigration
expected_behavior.en:
Across islands, immigration received per generation decreases with mean
distance to the other islands (correlation clearly negative, measured ~ -0.7).
expected_behavior.rationale:
migration_rate = 1/(1+distance) makes distant island pairs exchange fewer
migrants, so a more isolated island accumulates fewer arrivals — the
colonization gradient at the heart of MacArthur-Wilson island biogeography.

expected_behavior.name: migration-conserves-individuals
expected_behavior.en:
Inter-island migration conserves individuals exactly: the net migration flux
summed over all islands, species, and generations is zero.
expected_behavior.rationale:
Every emigration (-1 at the source) is matched by an immigration (+1 at the
destination), so the coupler is a pure exchange with no creation or
destruction of individuals.

behavior_tests.name: isolation-reduces-immigration
behavior_tests.description: Ensemble corr(immigration received, mean distance) must be below -0.3.

provenance.note:
Measured ~ -0.7 to -0.74 (8-island geometry, full-occupancy tally,
seed ensemble). -0.3 is a conservative negative ceiling.

behavior_tests.name: migration-conserves-individuals
behavior_tests.description: Total net migration flux over the ensemble must be ~0 (|flux| < 1e-9).

provenance.note:
Conservation is exact by construction: each migration event writes -1 to
the source and +1 to the destination of the same species.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
distance-immigration validates the migration coupler's kernel + conservation
independently of the per-island LV dynamics.

canonical_runs.name: default
canonical_runs.label: Migration kernel + conservation (8 islands, seed ensemble)
